help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The train's gone? Then we'll just take the next one. It'll be fine.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: That is true enough, but it doesn’t solve our problem.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: schon reassures: it will work out. eben signals resignation, and denn only colours questions.
help.tips[0].en.text: Dann bleiben wir eben zu Hause (well then, we'll just stay). Das ist halt so (that's just how it is). Das wird schon klappen (it'll work out, don't worry). Das ist schon richtig, aber … (that's true enough, but).
help.tips[0].en.title: Resignation: eben / halt; reassurance: schon
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: She'll probably come later. Don't you tell her anything – and do sit down already.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Go ahead and take another piece of cake.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: ruhig gives permission in a friendly way. wohl marks a guess, and denn doesn't go in commands.
help.tips[1].en.text: Er ist wohl krank (probably). Mach das bloß nicht! (don't you dare). Wenn er nur käme! (if only). Nimm ruhig noch ein Stück (go ahead, feel free).
help.tips[1].en.title: Guess: wohl; warning / wish: bloß, nur; permission: ruhig
help.tips[1].en.trap: wohl is not 'well'; bloß is not 'bare'; ruhig is not 'quietly' here; eben is not 'just now'. The particle meaning is separate from the adverb meaning of the same word.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: That's interesting! Go on, tell me what happened.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: What on earth is going on here?
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: To contradict a negative question ('Aren't you coming?' – 'Yes, I am!') German uses doch, not ja.
help.tips[2].en.text: doch: Setz dich doch! (encouraging) / Das ist doch teuer! (surprised contradiction) / Kommst du nicht? – Doch! (yes I do). ja: Das ist ja toll! (surprise at something evident) / Du weißt ja, … (as you know). mal: Komm mal her. denn: Was ist denn los?
help.tips[2].en.title: doch, ja, mal, denn — the familiar set, extended
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: Then we'll just do it like that, then.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: Particles sit in the middle field in a fixed order: doch before mal, never in first position.
help.tips[3].en.text: After the verb and the pronouns, before the rest: Komm doch mal her. Das ist ja wohl nicht dein Ernst. Fixed orders: ja doch, doch mal, eben mal, ja wohl. Always unstressed — stress the particle and it becomes its adverb again.
help.tips[3].en.title: Position and stacking
help.vocab[2].en: marks the known or the evident
help.context.en: What's up, then? – The bus has gone. – Then we'll just take a taxi, it'll be fine. – But that's far too expensive! – Oh, it's okay. Sit down, go on, I'll call one. – You know I don't like that. – I know. But don't you dare say you'd rather walk. It's probably going to rain any minute.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: Particles sit in the middle field, not first.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: Unstressed; bloß is the stronger warning.
help.hookEn: Tiny words like doch, halt and ruhig carry the tone of real conversation — add them and your German stops sounding like a textbook.
help.introEn: The modal particles, extended from the five you already know to the full spoken set. mal softens (Komm mal her; Warte mal); doch encourages, contradicts or expresses surprise (Setz dich doch! Das ist doch teuer! Das stimmt doch nicht!); ja marks the known or the surprising-but-evident (Du weißt ja …; Das ist ja toll!); eben and halt express resignation — that's just how it is (Dann bleiben wir eben zu Hause; Das ist halt so); schon reassures or concedes (Das wird schon klappen; Das ist schon richtig, aber …); wohl guesses (Er ist wohl krank); bloß / nur intensify a warning or a wish (Mach das bloß nicht! Wenn er nur käme!); ruhig permits (Nimm ruhig noch ein Stück); denn colours questions (Was ist denn los?). They sit in the middle field, unstressed, and can stack in a fixed order (ja doch, doch mal, eben mal). No particle is ever required by grammar — and their presence is what tells a listener you are at home in the language. Every real conversation, podcast and film dialogue is full of them.
help.rememberEn[0]: eben / halt = resignation; schon = reassurance; wohl = guess; bloß = warning; ruhig = permission.
help.rememberEn[1]: Middle field, unstressed, stackable (doch mal, eben mal).
help.recallEn.known: From "Modalpartikeln: denn, doch, eigentlich, ja, mal".
help.recallEn.today: halt, eben, schon, wohl, ruhig and bloß, and how they stack.
sentences[0].whyEn: mal makes the request small and casual.
sentences[4].whyEn: ja marvels at the evident: 'das ist ja …!'.
sentences[5].whyEn: eben/halt resign themselves to what can't be changed.
sentences[7].whyEn: schon/zwar concede before the aber arrives.
sentences[12].whyEn: denn makes the question curious and surprised.
sentences[14].whyEn: doch mal — doch encourages, mal keeps it casual.
sentences[15].whyEn: denn/bloß tint the question with reproach.
